title: Image of absolute Galois restriction for an arbitrary field inclusion
statement:
Let $K\subseteq L$ be fields [def-pc-field-extension]. Choose separable closures $K^s/K$ and $L^s/L$ [def-kun-separably-closed] and a compatible embedding $K^s\subseteq L^s$. Give $G_K=\operatorname{Gal}(K^s/K)$ and $G_L=\operatorname{Gal}(L^s/L)$ their Krull topologies, whose identity-neighbourhood bases are the subgroups fixing finite intermediate extensions pointwise. Put $E=K^s\cap L$ inside $L^s$. Restriction is a well-defined continuous homomorphism $r:G_L\to G_K$, its image is closed, and
$$r(G_L)=\{\sigma\in G_K:\sigma(e)=e\text{ for all }e\in E\}.$$
No algebraicity or separability of $L/K$ is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0BML (theorem-inifinite-galois-theory) and 0BMJ (lemma-galois-profinite), applied to the closed restriction image and its fixed field; Krull restriction continuity from the finite-subset neighbourhood basis.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois](2), with the intermediate field equal to the base, to both chosen closures: $K^s/K$ and $L^s/L$ are Galois. If $a\in K^s$, its minimal polynomial over $K$ splits in $K^s$. Every $\tau\in G_L$ fixes $K$ and sends $a$ to another root, hence into $K^s$. Applying this also to $\tau^{-1}$ proves $\tau(K^s)=K^s$. Restriction therefore defines $r:G_L\to G_K$, and $r(\tau\upsilon)(a)=\tau(\upsilon(a))=(r(\tau)r(\upsilon))(a)$.

source.place: Tag 030J, definition-separable-algebraic (normal and Galois); normality of the separable closures

proof.text: By [lem-exc-galois-krull-finite-limit], each of $G_K,G_L$ is topologically isomorphic to the compatible-family limit of its finite Galois groups, indexed by the nonempty directed set of finite Galois intermediate fields. Apply [lem-dl-a1-finite-group-limit-profinite] to these systems: both groups are compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological groups.

For a finite intermediate field F/K in Ks, use IntermediateField.essFiniteType_iff to choose a finite generating set S of F. Let T be its image in Ls and A = IntermediateField.adjoin L T. All elements of T are integral over L because Ls/L is algebraic, so Mathlib IntermediateField.finiteDimensional_adjoin makes A finite-dimensional. The open subgroup fixing A lies in the inverse image of the subgroup fixing F: fixing T implies fixing S after restriction, and hence fixing K(S)=F by forall_mem_adjoin_smul_eq_self_iff. Thus every identity neighbourhood has neighbourhood preimage, and continuous_of_continuousAt_one proves continuity. This directly uses the finite-algebraic-generation API instead of separately constructing the finite integral subalgebra and showing it is a field.

source.place: Tag 0BMJ, lemma-galois-profinite: Krull finite-subset neighbourhoods; finite algebraic generation made explicit

proof.text: By [lem-dl-a1-compact-hausdorff-closed-map], the continuous map $r$ from the compact space $G_L$ to the Hausdorff space $G_K$ has closed image. Thus $H=r(G_L)$ is a closed subgroup of $G_K$.

Apply [lem-exc-etale-galois-fixed-field-subgroup] to the Galois extension $L^s/L$ and its intermediate field $L$. Its full group $G_L$ has fixed field exactly $L$. Thus, for $a\in K^s$, being fixed by every element of $H$ is equivalent to being fixed by every $\tau\in G_L$ in $L^s$, and hence equivalent to $a\in L$. Therefore $(K^s)^H=K^s\cap L=E$. In particular $H$ fixes $E$ pointwise.

source.place: Tag 0BML, theorem-inifinite-galois-theory: base field equals full-group fixed field

proof.text: Package the closed range H as a ClosedSubgroup of Gal(Ks/K). Apply the closed-subgroup identity InfiniteGalois.fixingSubgroup_fixedField (already in the Mathlib attachment of lem-exc-etale-open-subgroup-fixed-field-galois) to obtain fixingSubgroup(fixedField H)=H. Substitute the elementwise fixed-field identification of the preceding step into mem_fixingSubgroup_iff. This proves exactly that H consists of automorphisms fixing the preimage of L. The general closed-subgroup correspondence proves this directly, so no separate intersection of open overgroups is needed. No algebraicity or separability assumption on L/K is introduced.
